correctness.rationale: Lattice normalization is the dual root lattice with rooted integer-coordinate differences and Euclidean quotient Jacobian 1/sqrt(n). For mQ, unique minimum normalized to zero gives the range<=m term (m+1)^n-m^n; any range>m must have a unique minimum/maximum at one of the 2k oriented missing matching pairs, with all remaining entries in [S-m,m], hence the exact sum 2k Σ h^{n-2}. The generating function gives Eulerian numerator, and classical Eulerian gamma expansion gives positivity. Continuous range decomposition with S in (1,t_j] integrates (2-S)^{n-2} separately for each pair, giving additive volume. Independently enumerated anchored integer potentials n=4..6,k=2..3,m=0..2; exact counts equal formula in all 12 profiles. This finite check is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The dual-lattice Ehrhart numerator and its gamma positivity are exact natural arithmetic invariants of a canonical family of graph metrics. Independent deformation of missing-pair lengths yields a nontrivial additive intrinsic-volume law, distinguishing disjoint from clustered edge deletion and useful for comparisons of graph Lipschitz polytopes.

final_claim: For n>=4, deletion of a matching of 2<=k<=floor(n/2) edges from K_n gives polar symmetric-edge-polytope Ehrhart polynomial in the dual root lattice A_{n-1}^*: (m+1)^n-m^n+2k sum_{h=1}^m h^{n-2}, and h*(z)=E_n(z)+2kzE_{n-2}(z), gamma-nonnegative. For each missing-pair metric length t_j in [1,2], intrinsic polar volume is [n+2/(n-1)*sum_j(1-(2-t_j)^{n-1})]/sqrt(n).
limitations: Exact lattice is A_(n-1)^*, not A_(n-1); euclidean volume is scaled by 1/sqrt(n) relative to rooted coordinates.
No overlapping deletions or length changes outside [1,2] are claimed.
Finite lattice checks are only consistency checks; full gamma and volume proofs are algebraic/measure arguments.
